title: Accessibility of a small-generated strongly saturated arrow class
statement: Use universes and presentable infinity categories from [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category] and coherent functor categories from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathcal C$ be presentable and let $S$ be a small set of its arrows. A class of arrows is replete if it is invariant under equivalence in $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)$. Let $W$ be the smallest replete class containing $S$ and all equivalences, closed under pushouts and all small colimits in $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)$, and satisfying two-out-of-three for composable arrows. Then the full subcategory $\mathcal A_W\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)$ spanned by $W$ is accessible. Its inclusion preserves all small colimits, which exist and are computed as in the ambient arrow category.

source.place: HTT Lemma 5.5.4.14, implication (3) to (1), printed pp. 480-481; colimit closure is part of strong saturation. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical theorem.

proof.text: Choose $\lambda<\kappa$ by [lem-coef-presentable-cardinal-enlargement]. In particular $\kappa$ is uncountable, $\lambda$ is sharply smaller in the explicitly stated cardinal sense, $\mathcal C$ is accessible at both cardinals, and all generator endpoints are $\kappa$-compact. Write $\mathcal E=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)$ and let $\mathcal D_0$ be the replete full subcategory of arrows of $W$ with $\kappa$-compact endpoints. It is essentially small: [lem-coef-presentable-cardinal-enlargement] bounds the equivalence classes of endpoints, and local smallness bounds the components of each mapping space of arrows between chosen endpoints. Colimits in $\mathcal E$ exist and are computed at the two endpoints by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. For a $\kappa$-small diagram in $\mathcal D_0$, its colimit arrow is in $W$ by the definition of $W$, and its two endpoints are $\kappa$-compact by [lem-coef-compact-small-colimits]. Thus $\mathcal D_0$ is closed under $\kappa$-small colimits.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.14, p. 480, choice of cardinal and compact-endpoint subcategory; Proposition 5.4.2.2(2).

proof.text: By the compactness clause of [lem-coef-accessible-diagram-presentations] with $K=\Delta^1$, all objects of $\mathcal D_0$ are $\kappa$-compact in $\mathcal E$. Define $\mathcal D_1$ as their replete full $\kappa$-filtered-colimit hull in $\mathcal E$. Applying [lem-coef-accessible-ind-colimit-extension] proves that $\mathcal D_1$ is $\kappa$-accessible and closed under all small ambient colimits, including the empty colimit. It also supplies a presentation of each object of $\mathcal D_1$ by $\mathcal D_0$ indexed by a small $\kappa$-filtered poset. The ambient category $\mathcal E$ is $\kappa$-accessible by [lem-coef-accessible-diagram-presentations] with $K=\Delta^1$ and has all small colimits by Step 1; it is therefore presentable by [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], as the hull lemma requires. Let $W_1$ be the arrows represented by $\mathcal D_1$.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.14, p. 480, filtered hull and its colimit closure.

proof.text: Every arrow of $\mathcal D_0$ belongs to $W$, and $W$ is closed under the filtered arrow colimits and equivalences used to form $\mathcal D_1$; hence $W_1\subseteq W$. The generator endpoints chosen in Step 1 are $\kappa$-compact, so $S\subseteq\mathcal D_0\subseteq W_1$. It remains to prove pushout stability and two-out-of-three for $W_1$. Its repleteness and closure under all small arrow colimits already follow from its definition and Step 2.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.14, p. 480, reduction to strong saturation.

proof.text: We establish a refinement procedure for either finite shape $K=\Lambda^2_0$ or $K=\Delta^2$. Start with a presentation of $p:K\to\mathcal C$ as a $\kappa$-filtered colimit of $q:N(A)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$ with pointwise $\kappa$-compact values; such a presentation exists by [lem-coef-accessible-diagram-presentations]. The procedure below applies to any such presentation, so a repeated application starts with the presentation produced by the preceding application. Fix an edge $e$ of $K$ whose value $p(e)$ belongs to $W_1$. Present $p(e)$ by $r:N(J)\to\mathcal D_0$ as in Step 2. Evaluation at $e$ preserves colimits by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], so $q_e$ and $r$ have equivalent total colimits in $\mathcal E$. Both take $\kappa$-compact values there by the compactness clause of [lem-coef-accessible-diagram-presentations] with $K=\Delta^1$: their two endpoints are $\kappa$-compact. For any subset $T\subseteq A$ of cardinality less than $\kappa$, apply [lem-coef-filtered-presentation-common-refinement] in $\mathcal E$ to $q_e,r$, with prescribed subsets $T$ and $\varnothing$. Obtain $\kappa$-small filtered subsets $A'\subseteq A$, $J'\subseteq J$ whose restricted edge colimits are equivalent. The colimit over $J'$ belongs to $W$; the colimit over $A'$ has $\kappa$-compact endpoints by [lem-coef-compact-small-colimits]. Thus the edge of $p_{A'}=\operatorname{colim}_{N(A')}q$ belongs to $\mathcal D_0$. Here the nerves are $\kappa$-small because $\kappa$ is uncountable regular and each finite chain is a finite tuple of fewer than $\kappa$ elements. Let $B$ be all $\kappa$-small filtered subsets $A'\subseteq A$ for which this edge of $p_{A'}$ lies in $\mathcal D_0$. Every $\kappa$-small subset $T$ is contained in some member of $B$. Consequently $B$ is $\kappa$-filtered: for fewer than $\kappa$ members, their union is $\kappa$-small by regularity, and the property just proved gives an upper bound in $B$; the empty collection is included. Also $A=\bigcup_{A'\in B}A'$. Every finite chain in $A$ is contained in one member, so $N(A)=\bigcup_{A'\in B}N(A')$. By [lem-coef-directed-cover-colimit-assembly] the diagrams $p_{A'}$ assemble coherently and have colimit $p$. Each is pointwise $\kappa$-compact by [lem-coef-compact-small-colimits]. If a second edge had already belonged to $\mathcal D_0$ at every stage of $q$, it still does at every stage $p_{A'}$, because $\mathcal D_0$ is closed under $\kappa$-small colimits. Thus this procedure can be repeated for a second designated edge while retaining the first.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.14, p. 481, construction of B from Lemma 5.5.4.13; directed assembly using Proposition 4.2.3.4 and Corollary 4.2.3.10.

proof.text: For a span $X'\leftarrow X\xrightarrow{f}Y$ with $f\in W_1$, apply Step 4 to its edge $f$. It becomes a $\kappa$-filtered diagram of spans $X'_b\leftarrow X_b\xrightarrow{f_b}Y_b$ with $f_b\in\mathcal D_0$ and all three vertices $\kappa$-compact. Pushout stability of $W$ puts $f'_b:X'_b\to X'_b\amalg_{X_b}Y_b$ in $W$. Its source is $\kappa$-compact and its target is $\kappa$-compact by [lem-coef-compact-small-colimits], so $f'_b\in\mathcal D_0$. The pushout arrow $f':X'\to X'\amalg_XY$ is the filtered colimit of these arrows. Indeed, write $\Lambda^2_0=N(A)$ for the span poset $A=\{a\le b,\ a\le c\}$ and $\Delta^1\times\Delta^1=N(A\cup\{d\})$ with $b,c\le d$; since $\mathcal C$ has finite colimits, [lem-coef-infinity-finite-poset-kan-extension] gives a functorial left adjoint $j_!$ of restriction, with $(j_!H)(d)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_A H$, so $j_!H$ is the pushout square of the span $H$ and its edge $b\to d$ is the pushout arrow. Apply $j_!$ to the $\kappa$-filtered diagram of spans: by the mapping-space adjunction and the colimit criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], $\operatorname{Map}(j_!\operatorname{colim}_b p_b,T)\simeq\lim_b\operatorname{Map}(p_b,j^*T)\simeq\lim_b\operatorname{Map}(j_!p_b,T)$ naturally in $T$, so $j_!$ preserves this colimit. Evaluation at the edge $b\to d$ preserves colimits, computed objectwise by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]; hence $f'\simeq\operatorname{colim}_b f'_b$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)$. Therefore $f'\in W_1$. Finally Step 2 supplies the initial arrow $0\to0$, and the pushout of $0\to0$ along $0\to X$ is $\mathrm{id}_X$. Every equivalence $f:X\to Y$ is equivalent to $\mathrm{id}_X$ in the arrow category, via the square with vertical edges $\mathrm{id}_X$ and $f$; repleteness then puts $f$ in $W_1$.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.14, p. 481, pushout argument with the colimit functor of Lemma 5.5.2.3 (here the finite-poset left Kan extension); Remark 5.5.4.6 for equivalences.

proof.text: Let $p:\Delta^2\to\mathcal C$ have edges $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\to Z$, and $h:X\to Z$, with its specified coherent composition $gf\simeq h$. If $f,g\in W_1$, apply Step 4 first to $f$ and then to $g$. This yields pointwise $\kappa$-compact triangles whose $f$- and $g$-edges are in $\mathcal D_0$. Two-out-of-three for $W$ puts their $h$-edges in $W$; compactness of the vertices puts these edges in $\mathcal D_0$. Their filtered colimit is $h$ by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], so $h\in W_1$. If $f,h\in W_1$, refine first the $f$-edge and then the $h$-edge; two-out-of-three in $W$ gives the $g$-edge at each compact stage, and evaluation gives $g\in W_1$ on taking the filtered colimit. If $g,h\in W_1$, refine first the $g$-edge and then the $h$-edge; two-out-of-three in $W$ gives the $f$-edge at each compact stage, and its filtered colimit gives $f\in W_1$. In both repeated refinements the preservation of the first edge is the last sentence of Step 4.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.14, pp. 481-482, all three two-out-of-three cases.

proof.text: The replete class $W_1$ contains $S$ and every equivalence, is closed under all small arrow colimits and pushouts, and satisfies two-out-of-three by Steps 2-6. The defining minimality of $W$ gives $W\subseteq W_1$; Step 3 gives the reverse inclusion. Thus $\mathcal A_W=\mathcal D_1$. Its accessibility and closure under all small ambient arrow colimits are Step 2. For each such colimit, fullness identifies the mapping-space universal property in the subcategory with the ambient one, so the inclusion preserves it and the colimits are computed as claimed.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.14 (3)⇒(1), conclusion; closure under colimits is Definition 5.5.4.5(2).

proof_origin.place: Lemma 5.5.4.14 (3)⇒(1), pp. 480-482; Step 4 expands the refinement and directed-assembly argument, and Step 6 writes all three cases.
